title: Time Intervals: Adding and Subtracting Minutes
seo_title: Grade 3 Time Intervals Worksheets: Adding and Subtracting Minutes (TEKS 3.7C)
standard_text: 3.7C determine the solutions to problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes using pictorial models or tools such as a 15-minute event plus a 30-minute event equals 45 minutes
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 time worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.7C: read a clock to the minute, how much time passes, add and subtract time intervals in minutes on a number line and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Add the minutes to put time intervals together.
key_sub: 1 hour = 60 minutes. A 15-minute event plus a 30-minute event is 45 minutes.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A time interval is how long something takes: 15 minutes, 40 minutes.
  • To add intervals, add the minutes: a 15-minute event plus a 30-minute event is 45 minutes. A number line with jumps helps.
  • 1 hour = 60 minutes, not 100. 75 minutes is 1 hour 15 minutes.
  • To find how much time is left or how much longer, subtract.

Examples

Example

Practice starts at 4:15 p.m. and lasts 35 minutes. When does it end?

4:15 + 15 minutes = 4:30

4:30 + 20 minutes = 4:50

Answer: 4:50 p.m.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking an hour is 100 minutes1 hour = 60 minutes. Count on to the next hour first.
Counting tick marks instead of jumpsCount the minutes each jump covers.
Adding when the problem asks how much is leftTime used up means subtract.

faq.a: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes using pictorial models or tools, such as a 15-minute event plus a 30-minute event equals 45 minutes.

faq.q: How do you add time intervals?
faq.a: Add the minutes. If the total is 60 or more, you can also say it in hours and minutes: 70 minutes is 1 hour 10 minutes.

faq.q: What tools help with elapsed time?
faq.a: A number line marked in minutes, or a clock you can move. Jump to the next 5 or 10 minutes, then to the hour.

faq.q: How is time tested on the STAAR?
faq.a: Word problems ask how long an activity lasts, when it ends, or how much longer one activity is than another.
